page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz with 2 threads per core. It is provisioned with 14.0 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor configuration includes a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. Architectural support includes AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instructions, though it lacks newer AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. There are zero dedicated GPUs, and no complimentary local storage or public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance.

Benchmark evaluation reveals modest single-threaded throughput balanced against consistent multi-core capacity. Single-core evaluations reflect lower-tier performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 951.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1112.99, alongside poor compression throughputs of 19.06 GB/sec in gzip and 7.32 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3. However, multi-threaded metrics place firmly in the middle 50% category, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 5976.0 and stress-ng multi-core registering 11755.88. The PassMark CPU score stands at 12708.86, accompanied by solid mid-range figures across Clang compilation (10292.0) and ray tracing (12187.0).

Memory throughput exhibits typical mid-tier behavior, achieving 84.99 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 44.82 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2000.87. Application-level metrics highlight capable serving capabilities, with static web serving hitting 9.59 GB/sec and Redis SET performance logging 10.92 million operations per second. For lightweight AI workloads, small 135M model inference delivers 510.22 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 168.59 tokens/sec for generation.

Given its lean 0.9 GB-per-vCPU ratio and the lack of included local storage, the primary tradeoff centers on memory footprint and absolute per-thread latency. From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the configuration delivers dedicated multi-threaded processing density without incurring expenses for excess memory capacity. This makes n1-highcpu-16 functionally appropriate for parallelized compute tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving frontends, and horizontally scaled batch processors that do not require extensive in-memory working sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 instance provisioned with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores, 2 threads per core) on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, backed by 14.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes no local storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark data shows modest single-core throughput, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 951.0, paired with solid middle-tier multi-threaded output, including a Geekbench multi-core mark of 5976.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12708.86. Application benchmarks reflect reliable throughput for network-facing and compute pipelines, logging 10.92 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.59 GB/sec in static web serving. Featuring a low memory-to-vCPU allocation of approximately 0.9 GB per thread, it offers resource-efficient dedicated compute density for distributed batch operations, software build pipelines, web serving, and stateless parallel processing workloads.
